description: Boron is a chemical element with symbol B and atomic number 5. In its crystalline form it is a brittle, dark, lustrous metalloid; in its amorphous form it is a brown powder. As the lightest element of the boron group it has three valence electrons for forming covalent bonds.
uses: The primary use of elemental boron is as boron filaments in high-strength materials. Boron is primarily used in chemical compounds, with about half of all production consumed globally as an additive in fiberglass for insulation and structural materials. It is also used in polymers and ceramics for high-strength, lightweight structural and heat-resistant materials, in borosilicate glass, as sodium perborate for bleaching, as a dopant in semiconductors, and in some boron-containing organic pharmaceuticals.
characteristics: Crystalline boron is silvery to black, extremely hard at 9.3 on the Mohs scale, and a poor electrical conductor at room temperature with electrical conductivity of 1.5 × 10−6 Ω−1 cm−1. It has a melting point above 2000 °C and is chemically inert and resistant to attack by boiling hydrofluoric or hydrochloric acid. Natural boron is composed of two stable isotopes: boron-11 (80.1%) and boron-10 (19.9%).
